caption: The drawing depicts a symmetrical decorative object composed of geometric shapes and stylized motifs. At the top center, there are two red and black birds facing away from each other, each standing on a circular design that includes segment patterns in red and black with white accents. Immediately beneath the birds and at the center, there is a large arch-shaped form divided into segments filled with alternating black and red coloring, outlined in white with a scalloped outer edge. Below this arch is a rectangular frame, predominantly red with black rectangles and white outlining. A large, nearly square, rectangular shape occupies the center, rendered in a faint grey wash to suggest a reflective surface, resembling a mirror. Flanking the square are two pairs of geometric triangular forms, colored in red and black, with additional white outline detailing. White, daisy-like flowers with a black center are placed at three of the four frame corners. At the bottom right of the page, there is a small, inset grayscale drawing depicting a close-up of string or rope tied to a rectangular frame, accompanied by handwritten descriptive notes. The overall composition makes use of red, black, and white colors, arranged in a symmetrical and balanced layout. The artist's name and location, "Maizel G. Claflin - Taos," is written below the primary image.
title: Tin Mirror Frame
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
